facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_比肩 (Metal carrying The Twin). Persona The Twin (比肩). Definition line: "Same nature, same register, the standard you hold yourself to". Keyword Independence, charge steady, poles catalyst Self-trust / friction Isolation. Family function: Body. Cost dimension: the standard held to oneself; company that truly matches is rare. Arena: mirrors, stride, equal measure, walking beside. Classical portrait: same nature, same register; the standard held to oneself; self-reliance that can wall others out. Ruled domains: Peers, Independence, Self-reliance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 劫财.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal precision amplifying Metal — same-polarity self-referencing loop".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Twin: a standing force that meets the world edge-first and equal. Nothing about you waits for permission. You hold your line the way a blade holds its shape, and you respect exactly the people who hold theirs. Company, for you, is two swords in one sheath: close, parallel, never fused."
- k2_functional: "Your energy is tempered and even: slow to tire, slow to bend, restored by solitary work."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Sealed-off","Rigid","Solitary"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Peers":"Your peers are fellow blades: rivals you respect, colleagues you measure against, friends won through tested mettle. Keep two or three whose standards match yours. Iron sharpens iron is not a proverb to you. It is your social life.","Independence":"Independence, in metal, is structural: you do not perform autonomy, you are made of it. Guard it without sealing it. A blade alone stays sharp but unused, and your edge exists for work that matters.","Self-reliance":"You carry your own weight and everyone can feel it. The practice to add is borrowing well: one tool, one favor, one opinion at a time. Even the finest steel was forged by other hands."}

- Sibling cell 金_劫财 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Competition hones you visibly. The rival’s number posted on your wall, the timed run against your own record, the deal chased sharper because someone else wants it: pressure grinds you finer instead of down, and your edge is renewed weekly, on purpose, against real resistance."

Core element Metal, energy element Metal. Law: Metal and Metal are the same element (the self pair). Relative to the core the energy is the self, so Metal is this core's Body. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Metal on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Metal as the Body is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_金's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You built your own standard and you keep it with no one watching. Making a thing yourself feels safer than being measured on it, so you would rather build slowly alone than quickly with help. Let one favour into the making, because a thing made alone costs you more than one made with help.

value_b.text: The rules you live by are the ones you made for yourself. Since Metal is short in you, you make your own strength and put owing no one ahead of being carried. Once in a while let yourself be carried, because you built the whole of yourself with no one placed to catch you.

value.text: Whenever something matters, you make it yourself before anyone can offer. Making it alone proves the standard is yours rather than borrowed, and going without help comes ahead of going to bed. You pay for everything self-made with the rest you never take, so ask for a hand before you run empty.

value.text: You hold everyone to the same measure you hold yourself. Fairness feels cleaner to you than favour, so being even with someone comes ahead of being easy on them. Now and again let a friend off the hook, since you keep everyone you measure at a set distance.

value_b.text: Your measure for yourself is your measure for everyone else. Being even matters to you more than being liked, so you give the fair answer instead of the kind one. Give the kind one first from time to time, because you meet few who match your measure and you want to keep them.

value.text: Whenever a friend falls short of the measure, you keep the measure rather than the friend. Holding everyone to one even measure keeps you honest, so the measure comes ahead of the company every time. Bend it once for someone you like, because you spend long stretches of your life without company that fits.

value.text: You get your strength back alone and lose it in company. Being seen while low feels like a debt you never repay, so you go quiet to recover instead of calling anyone. Let one person near you while you are low, because you recover slower alone than you need to.

value_b.text: Being alone is how you recover and being around people is how you spend. Since your Metal runs short, you guard the quiet that rebuilds you ahead of any invitation. Try one invitation while you are tired, and see whether company counts as rest for you.

value.text: Whenever you run low, you recover out of sight until you are whole again. Showing up half-built feels worse than showing up late, so you take the long quiet over the quick ask. Show someone the half-built version, as recovering alone costs you the friend who would have come.

value.text: Pulling away to recover alone spares the people close to you your worst days. Since you return rebuilt instead of being seen rebuilding, you give them the finished version and keep the work. Let them watch the work once, because you deny your closest people the chance to be needed by you.
